successors.name: Ubaid period
successors.text: northern Mesopotamia, which "showed Ubaidian characters" after the Halaf-Ubaid Transitional period

ledger.x: 6000 BCE: the painted-pottery villages of the Halaf hold the dry-farming belt of Upper Mesopotamia.
5450 BCE: Domuztepe, the largest Halaf settlement, is abandoned.
5350 BCE: the Halaf reaches the Tigris piedmont as the Hassuna villages end.
5100 BCE: the Halaf becomes the northern Ubaid.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: radii around excavated villages, never a frontier.
